# The nuxt-backend API

Every public name of the installed package, with the first sentence of its doc comment. The file
ships inside the package, so it describes exactly the version in `node_modules`.
[surface.json](surface.json) holds the same names as data, and [renames.json](renames.json) the
names a release renamed or removed; the `nuxt-backend-upgrade` skill lists them as a table. Each task
skill's own `references/api.md` has the part it covers. The docs: https://nuxt-backend.dev/docs/reference.

## Auto-imported composables

| Composable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `useAuth()` | Who is signed in: the session, the app-wide role, whether an administrator is visiting, and signing out. |
| `useConnectionState()` | The base module's, from `nuxt-convex-module/client`, under a neutral name. |
| `useBackendClient()` | The base module's, from `nuxt-convex-module/client`, under a neutral name. |
| `useLoginFlow()` | The headless login flow behind `<AuthForm>` — bring your own markup and wire these refs/actions to it. |
| `useEmailChange()` | The headless email change behind `<ProfileSettings>`: a code from the current address proves the person asking still holds it, a code from the new address proves they hold that one too. |
| `useWorkspace()` | Workspace state and actions: the list, the switch, the members and the full invitation flow (invite / accept / decline / cancel — the packaged `AcceptInvitation` component and `/accept-invitation` page build on these). |
| `useSearch()` | Reactive, debounced full-text search. |
| `useBilling()` | Reactive billing state plus the full subscription lifecycle — checkout, gift, portal, plan change and undoing a scheduled one, cancel/uncancel, pause/resume — linked to your auth user. |
| `useFeatures()` | Reactive feature-gating for the current user — the SaaS access primitive. |
| `useCredits()` | Reactive prepaid-credit balance for the current user, plus a `topUp()` checkout and a `refresh()` re-sync. |
| `usePricing()` | The app's plans and credit packs as a pricing page shows them — every plan with its monthly and yearly price, what a year saves, its trial and the credits it grants per cycle; every pack with its price per credit and which is the best value — read through the scaffolded `getPricing`, in the visitor's currency where the catalog prices it. |
| `useCampaign()` | The campaign a visitor arrived with, read from the address: a campaign link's discount code and its UTM attribution, ready for checkout. |
| `useOrders()` | The signed-in customer's billing history — past charges straight from the provider's orders API, plus the per-order invoice link. |
| `useUsage()` | Consumption history for a credit meter, read from the provider's events API — the events your server ingested when it spent credits. |
| `useGifts()` | Gifts, from both sides. |
| `useReferrals()` | A person's referral code, link and rewards: the data behind `<ReferralCard>`, for a page of your own. |
| `useReferralAdmin()` | The admin console's Referrals tab, as data: the program's totals, the top referrers, the flagged queue and one referrer's history, through `backend/referrals.ts`, and the decision an administrator makes on a flagged referral. |
| `usePasskeys()` | Passkey management over the auth client — list, register, rename, remove. |
| `useSessions()` | Device-session management: list, revoke one, revoke the rest. |
| `useReauthentication()` | Asking the person to confirm it is them before a sensitive action: the client half of `requireRecentSignIn` and of the routes that take a recent sign-in. |
| `useAuditLog()` | The activity trail, a page at a time: the signed-in account's own (sign-ins, passkeys, email and session changes, workspaces joined, an administrator's actions on it), the active workspace's for its owners and admins, or every event for administrators. |
| `useAccount()` | The account itself: its profile, its export and its deletion. |
| `useConsents()` | What a signed-in person agreed to, and the consent manager for optional storage. |
| `useAdmin()` | The admin console's data and actions: a paged, searchable list of every account or every workspace, one account or workspace in full, and the administrator's actions on an account. |
| `useFlag()` | Whether a feature flag is on for whoever is looking: their account, their active workspace and their plan, as `backend/flags.ts` declares the flag and the admin console overrides it. |
| `useFlagAdmin()` | The admin console's Flags tab, as data: every flag with its default and its override, and the change an administrator makes, through `listFlags` and `setFlag` of `backend/flags.ts`. |
| `useAccessPhase()` | The app's launch phase, so a page offers what a visitor can do now: join the waitlist in early access, bring an invite code while invite only, sign up once public. |
| `useInvite()` | Redeem an invite code or an access link on a page of your own: check it before anyone signs in, and keep it for the tab so the sign-in hands it over with the code. |
| `useAccessAdmin()` | The admin console's Access tab, as data: the launch phase and its change, the invite codes and access links, and the invitations by address, through `backend/access.ts`. |
| `useWaitlist()` | Join the waitlist, and read a place in it, on markup of your own: the steps `<WaitlistForm>` runs. |
| `useWaitlistAdmin()` | The admin console's Waitlist tab, as data: the waiting people (the oldest first, narrowed by a filter) with a count per status, and the changes an administrator makes, through `backend/waitlist.ts`. |
| `useShareLink()` | One row's share link: whether it has a live one and since when, read live, and the actions that turn it on (or mint a new one) and off, through `getShareLink`, `enableShareLink` and `revokeShareLink` of `backend/storage.ts`. |
| `useUploadField()` | The upload field without its markup: pick a file (by the button or by dropping it), upload it with the base module's `useUpload` through the upload URL `setupStorage` mints, then hand the storage id to your `claim`, where the deployment checks it. |
| `useNotifications()` | The signed-in account's in-app notifications, live: newest first, paged with `loadMore`, with the unread count and the actions that mark them read. |
| `useNotificationInbox()` | `<NotificationInbox>` without its markup: the notifications, where the inbox is, the button's name with the unread count in it, and the bindings for a button and a list that open on the browser's own popover. |
| `useEmailPreferences()` | The email topics the signed-in person receives and their notification channels, kind by kind, live, and the actions that change them: the same choices as the profile's Email section, the unsubscribe page and the provider's own page, which all stay in step. |
| `usePushSubscription()` | Web push on this device, for the signed-in person: whether the browser can take it, whether this device is subscribed, the permission, and the actions that subscribe and unsubscribe it. |
| `useAnnouncements()` | The announcements an administrator published that the signed-in person has not dismissed, live: what `<BackendNotices>`' `announcement` notice shows. |
| `useAnnouncementsAdmin()` | The admin console's Announcements tab, as data: every announcement with its notice and its broadcast, and the changes an administrator makes, through `backend/email.ts`. |
| `useContactForm()` | The contact form without its markup: a name and an address for a visitor, the message alone for a signed-in account (so the same form on a page behind sign-in is a feedback form), the bot check, a honeypot, and the deployment's refusals. |
| `useOnboarding()` | The first run at `/welcome` without its markup: the steps in order, where the person is, moving between them, and the stamp that ends it. |
| `useActivation()` | The activation checklist without its markup: the first tasks `defineActivation` declares, which of them are done, the progress, and dismissing it. |
| `useExperiment()` | The variant of an experiment, a `defineFlags` flag with `variants`, for whoever is looking. |
| `useAppShell()` | The app shell without its markup: who is signed in, the links of the account menu, signing out, and the workspace switcher. |
| `useInboxAdmin()` | The admin console's Inbox tab, as data: what people sent through the contact form and by email (reply addresses, workspace addresses, the support inbox), newest first, and the replies an administrator sends to the support inbox's threads, through `backend/email.ts`. |
| `getBackendError()` | Read a refusal out of anything a call threw or resolved with: a `backendError()` from a Convex function, the rate limiter's own `RateLimited` error, an auth client's `{ data, error }` result or its `error`, a Better Auth `APIError`, and any of these as an `Error`'s `cause`. |
| `useBackendConfig()` | `appConfig.backend` with the package defaults merged in — the shipped components read content (plan catalog, labels, brand) through this, so a partial user config is always safe to destructure. |
| `useLabels()` | The labels of one packaged component's group, resolved for the person reading them. |
| `useBackendPagePath()` | Where a ready-made page lives, for a link to it: the path the module mounted it at (the `pages` module option, else its default), in the active locale when the app uses `@nuxtjs/i18n` (through its `localePath`, so `/pricing` reads `/fr/pricing` under a prefix strategy). |
| `useReturnPath()` | Where the person goes once a page that interrupted them is done: the page they were headed for, from the `?redirect=` the sign-in and the first-run redirect carry (kept to a path on this site, so a link can never send them elsewhere), else where sign-in lands (`redirects.afterSignIn`, `/` without it). |
| `useEmailStatus()` | Reactive delivery status for a sent email. |
| `useSandboxInbox()` | The mail a test address received within the last hour, refreshed while the page is open — so a demo, a preview deployment or an e2e run can finish an email-code sign-in without a real mailbox. |
| `useWorkflowStatus()` | Reactively track a durable Workflow's status. |
| `useAiStream()` | Drive a metered, persisted AI text stream (an `ai.stream(...)` definition from `nuxt-backend/ai`). |
| `useJob()` | One queued job, live: its status, what holds it and its place in line while it waits, its progress while it runs, and its result or the reason it failed. |
| `useAiLabel()` | The AI-generated label without its markup: its words, and with a provenance record the details it opens — the models, the date and a link to check the content credentials — as state and bindings. |
| `useChat()` | A chat with a model, live: the person's threads, the open thread's messages with the reply streaming into them, and sending. |
| `useHumanCheck()` | Proof that a person makes a call: the client half of `verifyHuman`, for the calls that reach the deployment over the live connection and never pass through the app's server (a waitlist join, a contact form, a referral claim). |

The base module's, auto-imported under neutral names: `useQuery`, `useQuery_experimental`, `useQueries`, `useMutation`, `useAction`, `useUpload`, `uploadFile`, `useUploadQueue`, `useStorageUrl`, `usePreloadedQuery`, `useAsyncQuery`, `usePaginatedQuery`, `usePaginatedQuery_experimental`, `useAsyncPaginatedQuery`, `usePreloadedAuthQuery`, `resolveAuthRedirect`. Its
types, auto-imported too: `AsyncQueryData`, `AsyncQueryOptions`, `AsyncQueryReturn`, `AsyncQueryStatus`, `AsyncPaginatedQueryData`, `AsyncPaginatedQueryOptions`, `AsyncPaginatedQueryReturn`.

## Components

| Component | What it renders |
|---|---|
| `<AuthForm>` | The complete passwordless sign-in flow (passkeys + email OTP) in one component: semantic markup where every element carries a `data-auth` attribute, built from parts (`AuthFormChoose`, `AuthFormCode`, …) that a same-named component of the app's replaces, and a slot per step. |
| `<WaitlistForm>` | Join the waitlist: the address, your questions, the launch-news box (unticked), then the sign-in code that proves the address, then the person's place, a link to share and a way to leave. |
| `<ReauthenticateDialog>` | "Confirm it's you": the dialog a sensitive action opens when the server refuses it as `reauthentication_required`. |
| `<ProfileSettings>` | Account profile: identity chrome (avatar initials, verification / role / workspace badges), display-name editing, the email change, by a code from each address, and, with `@nuxtjs/i18n` and two locales or more, the person's language, which their emails are written in. |
| `<SecuritySettings>` | Everything that guards the account: passkey management (add / inline rename / remove), active device sessions (revoke one / revoke others), the latest sign-ins from a new device (each signs its session out while it lasts), and signing this browser out. |
| `<ConsentPrompt>` | Asks for the consents a person has not given at their current version, and nothing else: the required kinds `setupAccount({ consents })` declares after a version rises (the page waits behind a dialog until they are accepted), the age of an account that never answered the minimum age, and, while the app uses optional storage, one question per browser with **Allow** and **Decline** of equal weight. |
| `<OnboardingFlow>` | The first run a new account sees once, at `/welcome`: a few short steps. |
| `<ActivationChecklist>` | The first tasks that lead to value, with progress, for a page of your app: the tasks `defineActivation` declares, each ticked off when its event is recorded, "2 of 4 done", a link per open task and a Dismiss button. |
| `<HowDidYouHear>` | One optional question after sign-up: "How did you hear about us?". |
| `<AccountData>` | The account's data rights: download everything the app keeps of the account in one file, and delete the account, once the person typed their address to confirm it. |
| `<WorkspaceSettings>` | Workspace, plan, and credits management — the billing entity is the active workspace, so switching workspaces switches the subscription. |
| `<AcceptInvitation>` | Accept/decline UI for a workspace-invitation link (`/accept-invitation?id=<invitationId>` — the URL invitation emails point at). |
| `<AuditLog>` | The activity trail as a list, a page at a time: the signed-in account's own (`scope="mine"`, the default), the active workspace's for its owners and admins (`scope="workspace"`), or every event for administrators (`scope="all"`). |
| `<PricingTable>` | A complete pricing table, rendered on the server: plan cards from the live pricing (`usePricing`, the scaffolded `getPricing`), a monthly / yearly switch with what a year saves, subscribe / switch / cancel actions, credit packs compared credit for credit, a contact card, and a customer-portal link. |
| `<BillingCheckoutLink>` | A link that opens a checkout for the caller's billing entity. |
| `<BillingPortalLink>` | A link that opens the billing customer portal for the caller's billing entity, through the app's `generateCustomerPortalUrl`, on click. |
| `<BillingHistory>` | The customer's past charges with their invoice links — every row read live from the billing provider (this package stores no order ledger), so what renders is what the provider will show on the invoice. |
| `<UsageHistory>` | Metered consumption, event by event, straight from the provider's events API — the same records that drew the credit balance down. |
| `<UpgradePrompt>` | What someone whose plan lacks a feature sees: a sentence naming the plans on sale that include it, in pricing order, and a link to the first of them on the pricing page (`/pricing?plan=<key>`). |
| `<CancelFlow>` | Cancelling takes one step; a save offer is one optional step (LIFECYCLE). |
| `<WithdrawalButton>` | The EU withdrawal button (LIFECYCLE; Consumer Rights Directive Art. |
| `<ReferralCard>` | A person's referral link, with copy and share buttons and the disclosure of the reward: the link is `/r/<code>` on this site, made the first time the card is read. |
| `<AdminUsers>` | Every account of the app, for its administrators: a search by address, a page at a time (`AdminUsersTable`), and a drawer with one account in full (`AdminUserDrawer`): its role, its ban, its device sessions and workspaces, and "Impersonate". |
| `<AdminWorkspaces>` | Every workspace of the app, read-only, for its administrators: a search by name, a page at a time (`AdminWorkspacesTable`), and a drawer with one workspace's members and open invitations (`AdminWorkspaceDrawer`). |
| `<Gate>` | Renders its content only for the people every check it names admits: signed in (`signed-in`), an app-wide role (`role`), the active workspace or a role in it (`workspace`), a feature of the plan (`feature`), or room left on a quota (`quota`, `amount`). |
| `<BackendNotices>` | One region for every notice that holds for the whole session, on every page: an administrator acting as the account, maintenance, a failed payment, a scheduled deletion, low credits, a gift to claim and announcements. |
| `<AccessDenied>` | What a signed-in person sees when a page is not open to them: the page guard's 403 (`definePageMeta({ auth: { role, workspace, feature } })`) on the module's error page or your app's `error.vue`, or a refusal of your own. |
| `<ConnectionStatus>` | The live connection's state, in words, for a person: nothing while it is up; "Reconnecting…" once a drop has lasted `delay`; "You're offline." as soon as the browser is; and how many changes wait to be sent meanwhile. |
| `<UploadField>` | A labelled file field that uploads through the upload URL `setupStorage` mints, then calls `claim`, where the deployment checks the file. |
| `<NotificationInbox>` | What the app told a person, in the app: a button whose accessible name carries the unread count, and the list it opens on the browser's own popover, newest first. |
| `<ContactForm>` | A contact form for visitors, and a feedback form for signed-in people: the same component. |
| `<AppShell>` | The frame of a signed-in app, for your layout: a header with your brand and links, the workspace switcher, the notification bell and the account menu, then the app-wide notices, then your page in the `<main>` landmark, with the consent dialog and the connection status closing it. |
| `<AiLabel>` | The visible "AI-generated" label the EU AI Act (Art. |

The base module's, under neutral names: `<Authenticated>`, `<Unauthenticated>`, `<AuthLoading>`, `<AuthRefreshing>`, `<AuthBoundary>`, `<StorageImage>`.

## Server and route middleware

- Nitro auto-imports, in server code: `backendAuth`.
- Route middleware:  sends a signed-out visitor to sign in.
- The page guard (`backend-access`, global, so a page never names it in `middleware`): `definePageMeta({ auth: { role, workspace, feature, hidden } })` opens a page only to a signed-in person who passes every rule given; a signed-out visitor goes to sign in, and a signed-in one who fails gets a 403 whose `error.data.reason` names the rule.

## Pages

| Key | Default path | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `acceptInvitation` | `/accept-invitation` | Where an invited person accepts a workspace invitation (private). |
| `accessibility` | `/legal/accessibility` | The accessibility statement (public): the standard the app follows, how it is checked, and where to report a barrier, filled from `appConfig.backend.legal` and marked "not legal advice". |
| `admin` | `/admin` | The admin console: accounts, workspaces, the activity trail and the app's health (private and hidden: it answers 404 to anyone without the `admin` role). |
| `gifts` | `/gifts` | The gifts a person sent and received, with resend, change, cancel and claim (private). |
| `invite` | `/invite` | Where an access link lands (public, kept out of search indexes): it checks the link's token and sends the person on to sign in. |
| `keepAccount` | `/account/keep` | Where the "keep my account" link of a scheduled deletion lands (public, kept out of search indexes). |
| `login` | `/login` | The sign-in page (public, kept out of search indexes), and where the page guard sends a signed-out visitor. |
| `pricing` | `/pricing` | The pricing page (public). |
| `privacy` | `/legal/privacy` | The privacy policy (public): who runs the app, the data map, the subprocessors, the cookies and how a person exports or deletes their data, filled from `appConfig.backend.legal` and the capabilities the app uses, and marked "not legal advice". |
| `profile` | `/profile` | The account profile (private). |
| `referral` | `/r/:code` | Where a referral link lands (`/r/<code>`; public, kept out of search indexes): it says who invited the visitor and what they get, and signing up there claims the referral. |
| `report` | `/report` | The public notice form (DSA Art. |
| `security` | `/security` | Passkeys, sessions, account deletion and the account's recent activity (private). |
| `settings` | `/settings` | Workspace, plan and credit settings, and the workspace's activity for its owners and admins (private). |
| `subprocessors` | `/legal/subprocessors` | The subprocessor list (public): each service that processes personal data for the capabilities the app uses, what it handles, where, and its agreement; marked "not legal advice". |
| `terms` | `/legal/terms` | The terms of service (public): the company and contact, accounts and sign-in, plans and renewal, the merchant of record's role and the content rules, filled from `appConfig.backend.legal` and the capabilities the app uses, and marked "not legal advice". |
| `unsubscribe` | `/unsubscribe` | Where a topic email's unsubscribe link and a double opt-in's confirmation link land (public, kept out of search indexes and caches): one press leaves the topic, or confirms it. |
| `waitlist` | `/waitlist` | Where a waitlist status link lands (public, kept out of search indexes): a person's place in the line, read from the signed token in the link's fragment. |
| `welcome` | `/welcome` | The first run a new account sees once after its first sign-in: name, workspace, teammates and a plan, with steps of your own (private). |

### `nuxt-backend`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `default` | The Nuxt module: list `'nuxt-backend'` in `modules`. |

### `nuxt-backend/auth`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `APIError` | Re-exported from `better-auth/api`. |
| `resolveSignInMethod()` | The `customResolveMethod` of Better Auth's `lastLoginMethod` plugin that names a sign-in its own resolver does not know: a code sign-in (`/sign-in/email-otp`, which also signs a new account up) is `email-otp`. |
| `storesLastSignInCookie()` | Whether the browser that signs in allowed the `preferences` purpose of optional storage: its choice rides in a first-party cookie of the consent manager (`backend.storage`), which the request carries. |
| `setupAuth()` | The app's auth, from one call: the auth instance factory, the functions the scaffold re-exports. |

### `nuxt-backend/http`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `registerBackendRoutes()` | Mount every route the backend serves on the app's HTTP router: the auth routes, the billing and email webhooks, the metered AI stream, and the health. |

### `nuxt-backend/functions`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `BACKEND_ERRORS` | Every code the package throws, with the HTTP status an auth route answers it with and the validator its data is checked against where it is thrown. |
| `backendError()` | Build the error for a refusal: `throw backendError('forbidden', { reason: 'role' })`. |
| `getBackendError()` | Read a refusal out of anything a call threw or resolved with: a `backendError()` from a Convex function, the rate limiter's own `RateLimited` error, an auth client's `{ data, error }` result or its `error`, a Better Auth `APIError`, and any of these as an `Error`'s `cause`. |
| `RECENT_SIGN_IN_SECONDS` | How recent a sign-in a sensitive action takes, in seconds: ten minutes. |
| `SENSITIVE_ACTIONS` | The table, by Better Auth route (its path under the auth base path) or by scaffold function (`module:export`, as the client calls it). |
| `defineRetention()` | Delete a table's rows once they pass an age, a batch per transaction, until none is left. |
| `normalizeEmail()` | The address trimmed and lower-cased: the form to store and compare it in, so `Ana@Example.com ` and `ana@example.com` are one person. |
| `randomToken()` | A random token from the platform's secure random source: 32 bytes by default, written as 43 URL-safe characters (`A-Z a-z 0-9 - _`), so it goes into a path or a query as it is. |
| `sha256Hex()` | The text's SHA-256 as 64 lower-case hex characters, from its UTF-8 bytes. |
| `createFunctions()` | Every access tier of your backend, from one call in `backend/functions.ts`: each a drop-in `{ query, mutation, action }` that checks the caller before the handler runs. |
| `verifyHuman()` | Check that a call comes from a person, in a function of your own: a waitlist join, a contact form, a referral claim, any call that reaches the deployment over the live connection and never through the app's server. |

Types: `BackendError`, `BackendErrorArgs`, `BackendErrorCode`, `BackendErrorData`, `BackendErrorPayload`, `RetentionArgs`, `RetentionOptions`, `RetentionResult`, `SensitiveAction`, `SensitiveLimit`, `AuthorizationComponents`, `AuthorizationCtx`, `FunctionUser`, `AuthorizationWorkspace`, `CallerRule`, `FunctionWorkspace`, `FunctionDeclaration`, `FunctionsRateLimiter`, `FunctionsBilling`, `FunctionsComponents`, `CreateFunctionsOptions`.

|---|---|
| `ALL_EMAIL_EVENTS` | The provider's full webhook event catalog: every transactional delivery state, plus the contact and domain events the marketing surface (segments/contacts/broadcasts) generates. |
| `setupEmail()` | App-facing email helper over the `backend` component's email module: both **transactional** email (send / status / cancel + webhook) and **marketing** email (segments / contacts / broadcasts via the provider SDK). |
| `escapeHtml()` | Escape text for HTML: `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`. |
| `forceColorScheme()` | A rendered email as a reader in `scheme` sees it, whatever the previewing page prefers: `dark` applies the layout's dark styles unconditionally, `light` drops them. |
| `html()` | A tagged template for an email's HTML: every value it interpolates is escaped (`escapeHtml`), so a name or anything else a user typed cannot put markup into an email your domain sends. |
| `trustedHtml()` | Mark markup as safe for `html` to insert unescaped: a fragment you built with `html` itself, or markup of your own that holds nothing a user typed. |
| `describeOrigin()` | Where a request came from, in the reader's language: `Requested from Chrome on macOS, near Lisbon, Portugal, at 27 Oct 2026, 14:02 WET.` Each part the request did not give is left out; the time is always there, in the requester's time zone when the host named one, else in UTC. |
| `linkBlocks()` | The blocks of an email's one link: a button, then the link written out for a mail app that shows no button (the `email.link.fallback` label). |
| `plainName()` | A name someone typed as an email shows it: every link and bare domain taken out, whitespace collapsed, at most `max` characters; `undefined` when nothing is left. |

## CLI

### `npx nuxt-backend init`

Scaffold the backend files, .env.example, and nuxt.config wiring (re-run to restore missing files; --force to reset).

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--force`: Overwrite existing scaffold files and .env.example, replace AGENTS.md's nuxt-backend section, and replace or remove agent skill copies another version wrote
- `--agents`: Coding-agent files: --agents rewrites only AGENTS.md's nuxt-backend section, .mcp.json and the agent skills in .agents/skills for the installed version, and adds the MCP SDK to devDependencies when missing; --no-agents skips them all
- `--no-agents`: Coding-agent files: --agents rewrites only AGENTS.md's nuxt-backend section, .mcp.json and the agent skills in .agents/skills for the installed version, and adds the MCP SDK to devDependencies when missing; --no-agents skips them all
- `--json`: Machine-readable output

`--json`: `{ created, agentsMd, mcpJson, skills, appComponent, devScript, convexDependency, mcpSdkDependency, nuxtConfig, next }`, or `{ agentsMd, mcpJson, skills, mcpSdkDependency }` with `--agents`, where `skills` is `{ installed, refreshed, removed, stale }`, each a list of skill names; progress goes to stderr.

### `npx nuxt-backend dev`

Run Convex and Nuxt together: set up the dev deployment on the first run, provision its env, then `convex dev --start "nuxt dev"` (other arguments go to nuxt dev).

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--anonymous`: Start on an account-free local deployment, with no Convex login and no question, on every OS

`--json`: none: it runs until stopped, with Convex and Nuxt printing to the terminal.

### `npx nuxt-backend doctor`

Check the project + deployment configuration.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--json`: Machine-readable output
- `--fix`: Repair what doctor can: restore missing scaffold files, add missing mounts and routes, push env (`env push`), at a terminal make the first administrator, and apply the provider settings the billing findings recommend and turn a webhook endpoint back on, each after you confirm it
- `--yes`: With --fix: apply the provider changes without asking (for a script or CI)
- `--prod`: Check the production deployment: missing email/billing config becomes a failure, its switches and email are read, and its live site is probed
- `--only`: Check only these capabilities, comma-separated: auth, data, jobs, billing, email, notifications, ai, protection, monitoring, flags, analytics, hosting

`--json`: `{ $schema, findings, summary }`, described by https://nuxt-backend.dev/schemas/doctor.json; with `--fix`, the repair's progress goes to stderr.

### `npx nuxt-backend status`

Show each capability's state — live, test, missing or failing — with its providers, unset env and most pressing finding.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--json`: Machine-readable output
- `--prod`: The production deployment's capabilities, under doctor's production posture and its live probes

`--json`: `{ deployment, status, capabilities: [{ name, title, state, reason, providers, missingEnv, findings, top, docsUrl, devtools }], summary }`: `state` is `live`, `test`, `missing` or `failing`, `status` is `ok`, `degraded` or `failing`.

### `npx nuxt-backend env push`

Sync backend env from .env(.local) to the Convex deployment (dev deployments also get AUTH_SECRET/SITE_URL provisioned).

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--prod`: Act on the production deployment; never invent values; fail on missing required env
- `--preview`: Act on the preview deployment of this name (empty: the branch the CI build names, as convex deploy does); fills AUTH_SECRET, test-mode email and sandbox billing
- `--defaults`: Write the project env defaults new deployments of this type start with: preview or dev
- `--site-url`: The SITE_URL to write, replacing the one already set (a preview's own origin)
- `--dry-run`: Print the plan without setting anything
- `--force`: Replace values already on the deployment with the local ones: a comma-separated list of names, or every name but BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT when bare (or "all"), which --prod refuses
- `--json`: Machine-readable output

`--json`: `{ deployment, dev, results: [{ name, action, detail, outcome, error }], missingRequired }`: `deployment` names what was written (`dev:<slug>`, `production`, `preview:<name>`, `defaults:<type>`); values never appear.

### `npx nuxt-backend env rotate`

Rotate AUTH_SECRET, EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET or BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET with no downtime: the new value beside the old, then the old retired.

- `<name>`: The secret: AUTH_SECRET, EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET or BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET
- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--prod`: Rotate production's secret
- `--dry-run`: Print each step it would take, and change nothing
- `--retire`: AUTH_SECRET: retire the old value now, not after the 30-day window (after a leak)
- `--json`: Print the outcome as one JSON document; progress goes to stderr

`--json`: `{ name, deployment, dryRun, steps: [{ step, outcome, note? }], state, retiresAt? }`: the steps it took and the secret's new state; values never appear.

### `npx nuxt-backend billing sync`

Push backend/billing.catalog.ts — meters, custom fields, feature/credit benefits, plans (a product per monthly and yearly price, trials, usage prices, tax behaviour; retired plans archived) and packs — to the billing provider, store the webhook endpoint's secret on the deployment, write billing.generated.ts (find-or-create, never deletes; drift reported) and load the deployment's products. Sandbox writes the deployment .env.local names; production writes the production deployment.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--env`: Target environment: sandbox | production (default: the environment the deployment bills in, read from its BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT, else sandbox)
- `--dry-run`: Print the plan without creating anything
- `--webhook`: Provision the webhook endpoint at this URL (default: <site>/billing/events of the deployment written; pass "off" to skip)
- `--force`: Store the webhook endpoint's secret even over a BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET the deployment already holds
- `--adopt`: Adopt existing objects (products, meters, custom fields): key=<id>[,key=<id>…] — recorded as-is, benefits untouched
- `--json`: Print the outcome as one JSON document; progress goes to stderr

`--json`: { environment, dryRun, deployment, log: [{ action, kind, key, id?, note? }], generated, webhook: { url, action: "created" | "exists" | "would-create" | "skipped", secret: "stored" | "kept" | "not-stored" | "none", note? }, products: { status: "synced" | "failed" | "skipped", note? } }.

### `npx nuxt-backend email sync`

Create the email topics, the accounts' segment and the contact properties backend/email.ts declares at the email provider, point the deployment's webhook at every event the package reads (storing a new webhook's secret), read each sender's region and DMARC, and sync the support inbox.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--prod`: Sync production's email account and write the production deployment
- `--dry-run`: Print each step it would take, and change nothing
- `--webhook`: Point the webhook at this URL (default: <site>/email/events of the deployment written; "off" to leave it alone)
- `--json`: Print the outcome as one JSON document; progress goes to stderr

`--json`: `{ deployment, dryRun, log: [{ action, kind, key, id?, note? }], webhook: { url, action, secret: "stored" | "not-stored" | "none" }, senders, region, inbound: { support, inbox, domain, webhook, todo } | null }`, the secret never in it.

### `npx nuxt-backend inbox`

Print the sign-in codes a dev deployment sent to a sandbox address (default delivered@resend.dev).

- `<address>`: The sandbox address to read, such as delivered+agent@resend.dev
- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--json`: Machine-readable output
- `--prod`: Refused: the inbox is read on dev deployments only

`--json`: `{ address, deployment, messages: [{ from, subject, receivedAt, code }], code }`: newest first, `code` the newest message's; bodies are never printed.

### `npx nuxt-backend upgrade`

Move the app to the installed version: repair the scaffold as doctor --fix does, and run the package's data migrations. It rewrites none of the app's code.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--dry-run`: Show what the scaffold repairs would change, as diffs, and where the data migrations stand; write nothing
- `--diff`: Print the upstream changes to each ejected file, or to the one named, as a unified diff; write nothing
- `--prod`: Run the data migrations on the production deployment; needs --yes
- `--yes`: Confirm --prod: the production data is migrated
- `--json`: Machine-readable output

`--json`: `{ to, dryRun, scaffold: { written, changes, diffs }, ejected: [{ target, file, from, to, changes }], data: { deployment, state, reason, migrations }, next }`: `data.state` is `done`, `running`, `pending`, `none`, `skipped`, `needs-push` or `failed`; `scaffold.diffs` comes with `--dry-run` only; with `--diff`, `[{ target, file, from, to, changes, diff }]` alone; progress goes to stderr.

### `npx nuxt-backend eject`

Copy a part's, a page's or an email's packaged source into the app, stamped with its version, so the app owns it.

- `<target>`: A part or a component (`PricingPlanCard`), `page:<key>` or `email:<name>`
- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--list`: Print every name it can eject, and change nothing
- `--force`: Overwrite a file of that name already in the app
- `--json`: Machine-readable output

`--json`: each file it wrote, with the version stamped in it: `{ target, version, written, todo? }`; with `--list`, `[{ target, kind, ejected }]`.

### `npx nuxt-backend deploy`

Take production from nothing to a passing doctor --prod: link or create the production deployment, push its env, push the backend, sync the billing catalog, register both webhooks, write the app's env into the Vercel project, then run doctor --prod. Safe to run again.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--dry-run`: Print every step it would take, and change nothing
- `--sandbox`: A demo or staging app: set BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox instead of production, and sync to the providers' test modes
- `--build`: Run as the host's build command: put the env the first push needs on production (AUTH_SECRET, SITE_URL from the host), then convex deploy builds the app against the backend
- `--json`: Print the outcome as one JSON document; progress goes to stderr

`--json`: `{ dryRun, environment, host, steps: [{ id, capability, title, outcome, detail }], doctor }`: `outcome` is `done`, `unchanged`, `planned`, `skipped` or `failed`, `doctor` is `{ pass, warn, fail, failing }` or null; values never appear.

### `npx nuxt-backend analyze`

Measure the backend's Convex bundle and the Nuxt app's client and server bundles: the largest packages, the share nuxt-backend and your code bring, and the insights that would shrink them. --max-convex, --max-client and --max-server fail a bundle over its budget.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--only`: Measure one half: convex (seconds, no Nuxt build) or nuxt
- `--max-convex`: Fail when the Convex bundle's code, without source maps, is larger (8MB, 500kB)
- `--max-client`: Fail when the Nuxt client bundle is larger
- `--max-server`: Fail when the Nuxt server bundle is larger
- `--json`: Print the report as one JSON document; progress goes to stderr

`--json`: `{ version, ranAt, bundles: [{ id, title, bytes, gzipBytes, sourceMapBytes, parts, packages, shares, insights, notes }], budgets: [{ bundle, flag, limit, bytes, over, grew }], failures: [{ half, message }] }`: `id` is `convex`, `client` or `server`, and `bytes` is the code without source maps; progress goes to stderr.

### `npx nuxt-backend mcp`

Run the developer MCP server for your coding agent over stdio: the project's state, the docs, and the Convex, billing, email and hosting consoles on your own logins; every tool that writes asks you first.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--prod`: Read production: the project, billing, email and hosting tools read it, the data tools read only its logs and insights, and every write is refused

`--json`: none: it speaks MCP on stdin and stdout until the client closes it.

## Error codes

A refusal is a `ConvexError` with one of these codes; `getBackendError(error)` reads it.

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | Nobody is signed in, or the session is gone. |
| `forbidden` | 403 | Signed in, but not allowed; `reason` says why (`banned`, `role`, `permission`, `not_member`, `workspace_role`, `admin_only`, `not_owner`, `impersonating`, `admin_target`, `sign_in_refused`, `customer_taken`, `already_subscribed`, `not_billing_manager`, `provider_owner_only`, `gift_refused`, `gift_refunded`, `not_recipient`, `no_email`, `bot_check`, `other_account`, `flag_off`, `sole_owner`, `paid_subscription`, `ticket_required`, `invitation_refused`, `consent_required`, `age_required`, `under_age`, `passkey_only_admin`). A `consent_required` refusal also carries `kind`, the required consent not yet accepted at its latest version. A `ticket_required` refusal also carries `phase`, the launch phase that asks for a ticket, and `invite`, how the invite code given checked (`expired`, `used-up`, `revoked`, `unknown`), when one was. |
| `reauthentication_required` | 403 | The call is a sensitive action, and the session's sign-in is older than it takes: sign in again (`useReauthentication`), then retry. Better Auth's own refusals of a session too old for its route read as this code too. |
| `no_workspace` | 409 | The call needs an active workspace and there is none. |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | A named limit is spent; `retryAfter` is in milliseconds. The job queue's budget (`limit: 'jobBudget'`) also names the `plans` on sale whose tier would fit the job now, in pricing order. |
| `insufficient_credits` | 402 | The balance can't cover the spend. |
| `feature_required` | 402 | The billing entity's plan does not include the feature the call needs; `plans` names the catalog plans on sale that do, in pricing order (none when no plan on sale includes it). |
| `quota_exceeded` | 402 | The billing entity's plan allows `limit` of the `quota`, `used` are held, and `amount` more do not fit; `plans` names the catalog plans on sale that allow enough, in pricing order. |
| `invalid_input` | 400 | An argument the call refuses; `field` names it, and `reason` says why when the field alone does not (`otp_expired`, `passkey_cancelled`, `no_password`, `retired`, `has_account`). A job bigger than any budget of the queue is `over_budget` on `cost`, with its `need` and the owner's `units`; a step's model refusing the content is `content_blocked` on `prompt`. |
| `not_ready` | 409 | There is nothing to act on yet, and retrying will not change that: `reason` says what has to happen first (`no_customer`, `not_synced`, `no_catalog`, `not_paid`, and `no_budget`: AI on a sandbox deployment whose `setupAi` sets no `spendLimit`). |
| `unavailable` | 503 | A service can't serve the call; `service` and `reason` say which and why. Only `provider_refused` may pass on a retry; the others need the deployment fixed, but a kill switch's (`signups_paused`, `checkout_paused`, `ai_paused`, service `signups`, `checkout` or `ai`), which an administrator turns off. Nothing throws service `backend` with reason `unexpected`: it is how a composable's `error` reads a failure without a code (a crash, an app's own error), and says nothing about whether a service is down. |

## Capabilities

The app's parts, each detected as `live`, `test`, `missing` or `failing`: `npx nuxt-backend status` shows them, and `doctor --only <capability>` checks one.

| Capability | Gives the app | Env |
|---|---|---|
| `auth` | Sign-in by email code and passkey, sessions, workspaces with roles and invitations, the admin console with impersonation, the activity trail, and each account's data export and complete erasure. | `AUTH_SECRET`, `SITE_URL` |
| `data` | The database with realtime queries, server rendering, full-text search, aggregates, counters and file storage. | `NUXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL`, `BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT` |
| `jobs` | Scheduled jobs, durable workflows, queued work, cached action results, migrations and the backend's own hourly maintenance. |  |
| `billing` | Plans with monthly and yearly prices, prepaid credits, a server-rendered pricing page, feature gates, gifts and the customer portal, from a catalog in code. | `BILLING_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET` |
| `email` | Transactional and marketing mail from one template registry, with delivery tracking and the dev inbox. | `EMAIL_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `EMAIL_MARKETING_FROM`, `EMAIL_REGION`, `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `EMAIL_DEV_INBOX` |
| `notifications` | An in-app inbox for every event the backend records about a person and for events of your own, live and in each person's language, with the unread count and marking read; the kinds that allow it by email, and as web push to each device a person allowed, under their channel choices. | `PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY`, `PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY` |
| `ai` | Metered model calls and streams: each call reserves prepaid credits, runs the model by its provider/model id, then settles at the cost it reports. | `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, `PROVENANCE_PRIVATE_KEY`, `PROVENANCE_CERTIFICATE` |
| `protection` | Bot checks on the requests that send a sign-in code or create an account, and on the calls of your own that verifyHuman guards. | `PROTECTION_PROOF_SECRET`, `PROTECTION_CHALLENGE_SECRET_KEY`, `NUXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_CHALLENGE_SITE_KEY` |
| `monitoring` | Error reports from the browser, the Nuxt server and the backend's actions, cron check-ins, and a health endpoint for uptime checks. | `MONITORING_DSN` |
| `flags` | Feature flags read inside queries and mutations, targeted by account, workspace, plan or a stable percentage, and the kill switches that pause sign-ups, checkout and AI or put up a maintenance banner. |  |
| `analytics` | Revenue metrics in the admin console: recurring revenue, subscriptions and churn with cancellations per reason, checkouts, usage per meter, and costs and margin, read live from the billing provider. |  |
| `hosting` | The app on its host: one-command production, the app's env written into the host, and the live site's HTTPS, security headers, backend and docs for agents checked. |  |

## Environment

| Name | Capability | Read on | Tier | Without it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_SECRET` | auth | deployment | required | a deploy fails: it signs sessions and encrypts the keys the session tokens are signed with |
| `SITE_URL` | auth | deployment | required | a deploy fails: auth trusts it as the app origin, and every emailed link names it |
| `BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT` | data | deployment | optional | every provider stays in its test mode, nothing local is trusted and no sign-in code is logged; `doctor --prod` fails on production |
| `EMAIL_API_KEY` | email | deployment | optional | email sends no-op; on `development` the sign-in codes print in the dev console, and elsewhere a code to a real address is refused |
| `EMAIL_FROM` | email | deployment | optional | the provider onboarding sender is used |
| `EMAIL_MARKETING_FROM` | email | deployment | optional | marketing mail goes from EMAIL_FROM |
| `EMAIL_REGION` | email | deployment | optional | the provider's default region |
| `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | email | deployment | optional | delivery events are rejected — useEmailStatus stays at "sent" |
| `EMAIL_DEV_INBOX` | email | deployment | dev-only | the dev inbox's page reader (getSandboxInbox, behind useSandboxInbox) answers nothing; the CLI's inbox still reads |
| `BILLING_ACCESS_TOKEN` | billing | deployment | optional | billing queries return empty and checkout actions fail on invocation |
| `BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | billing | deployment | optional | billing events are rejected — entitlements refresh only on demand (syncEntitlements) |
| `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` | ai | deployment | optional | a provider/model id the backend names goes through the Convex AI Gateway alone, on Convex Cloud with a paid plan and @convex-dev/ai-sdk-provider installed; anywhere else (a free plan, a self-hosted deployment) it is refused when called |
| `PROVENANCE_PRIVATE_KEY` | ai | deployment | optional | generated images are stored with the IPTC source type and no signed C2PA manifest (`ai.provenance_unsigned`); `doctor --prod` fails once the backend turns provenance on |
| `PROVENANCE_CERTIFICATE` | ai | deployment | optional | as without PROVENANCE_PRIVATE_KEY: the two sign together |
| `PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY` | notifications | deployment | optional | the in-app inbox and email notifications work, but web push does not: `getPushConfig` answers no key, so `usePushSubscription` reads unsupported |
| `PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY` | notifications | deployment | optional | as without PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY: the two sign together |
| `PROTECTION_PROOF_SECRET` | protection | both | optional | the auth routes that send a code take no proof of a bot check: on Vercel, BotID still refuses the bots that come through the app, but not the ones that call the deployment's own URL |
| `PROTECTION_CHALLENGE_SECRET_KEY` | protection | deployment | optional | the deployment verifies no challenge answer, so off Vercel nothing checks for bots |
| `MONITORING_DSN` | monitoring | deployment | optional | the backend reports nothing: errors in its actions and its cron check-ins go nowhere (the browser and the Nuxt server report on the DSN the app reads, and in dev a local error log stands in) |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL` | data | app | optional | derived from the deployment the platform CLI names in .env.local; set it to point at another deployment |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_CHALLENGE_SITE_KEY` | protection | app | optional | no challenge widget renders, so the deployment's PROTECTION_CHALLENGE_SECRET_KEY refuses every code request that carries no proof |

## The scaffold's function contract

The composables call these functions by name; keep them exported from the scaffolded files.
Names agents guess instead: `api.auth.getAuthUser`, not `api.auth.getCurrentUser`; `api.billing.getCurrentSubscription`, not `api.billing.getSubscription`; `api.billing.getCredits`, not `api.billing.getBalance`.

- `backend/auth.ts`: `getAuthUser`, `authConfig`, `updateProfile`, `listSessions`, `revokeSession`, `listSignInAlerts`
- `backend/billing.ts`: `generateCheckoutLink`, `generateCustomerPortalUrl`, `getConfiguredProducts`, `getPricing`, `listAllSubscriptions`, `giftCheckout`, `getCurrentSubscription`, `getFeatures`, `getBillingAccess`, `getCredits`, `syncEntitlements`, `syncProducts`, `startFreePlan`, `getReceivedGifts`, `claimGift`, `getSentGifts`, `resendGift`, `changeGiftRecipient`, `rescheduleGift`, `cancelGift`, `runGiftSweep`, `updateSubscription`, `cancelSubscription`, `acceptSaveOffer`, `getWithdrawal`, `withdraw`, `uncancelSubscription`, `cancelPendingChange`, `pauseSubscription`, `resumeSubscription`, `getOrders`, `getInvoiceUrl`, `getUsageHistory`, `refundOrder`
- `backend/email.ts`: `getEmailStatus`, `previewEmails`, `sendEmailPreview`, `getEmailPreferences`, `setEmailTopic`, `unsubscribeAllTopics`, `getEmailLink`, `unsubscribeByLink`, `confirmEmailTopic`, `recordTimeZone`, `syncEmail`, `getAnnouncements`, `dismissAnnouncement`, `getAnnouncementsConsole`, `publishAnnouncement`, `endAnnouncement`, `previewAnnouncement`, `sendAnnouncement`, `cancelAnnouncement`, `getSuppressions`, `liftSuppression`
- `backend/audit.ts`: `listActivity`, `listWorkspaceActivity`, `listAllActivity`, `getActivation`, `dismissActivation`
- `backend/notifications.ts`: `listNotifications`, `getUnreadCount`, `markNotificationsRead`, `getNotificationChannels`, `setNotificationChannel`, `getPushConfig`, `subscribePush`, `unsubscribePush`, `deliverNotification`
- `backend/account.ts`: `exportAccountData`, `getAccountExport`, `eraseAccountData`, `getConsents`, `getConsentTerms`, `grantConsent`, `withdrawConsent`, `chooseStorage`, `getAccountDeletion`, `cancelAccountDeletion`, `getOnboarding`, `completeOnboarding`
- `backend/admin.ts`: `listUsers`, `getUser`, `listWorkspaces`, `getWorkspace`
- `backend/flags.ts`: `getFlags`, `listFlags`, `setFlag`, `exposeExperiment`
- `backend/webhooks.ts`: `getWebhookDeliveries`, `replayWebhookDelivery`
